report.tagline: A Swedish AI tool that builds working web apps from a plain-English chat, so people who cannot code can ship software.
report.simpleSummary: Lovable lets you build an app by describing it in a chat. You type something like 'a booking app for my yoga studio with payments', and in a minute you see a working website you can click through. You keep chatting to change it, then publish it with one click. It is aimed at founders, designers and business people who cannot code, and it became one of the fastest-growing software companies ever.

overview.whatItDoes: Lovable turns a written idea into a full web app: screens, buttons, database, logins and payments. The AI writes real code (React and TypeScript) that you own. You can edit by chatting, by clicking on parts of the page, or by opening the code.
howItWorks: You describe your app in a chat box, or upload a screenshot or Figma design.
The AI writes the code and shows a live preview in seconds.
You ask for changes in plain words, or click on an element to edit it visually.
Lovable Cloud adds a database, user logins, file storage and AI features without setup; Supabase and Stripe are built in.
One click publishes the app to a web address; you can connect your own domain and sync code to GitHub.
Each message uses credits; paid plans give more credits a month.
overview.valueProposition: Go from idea to a live app in an afternoon, without hiring developers or learning to code.

businessModel.summary: Lovable sells monthly subscriptions that include a set number of credits. Each chat message uses credits. Heavier users buy bigger plans or top-ups. Companies pay for Business and Enterprise plans with team features and security. Lovable also earns from cloud hosting and AI usage inside apps built on Lovable Cloud.

revenueStreams.detail: From about $25 a month for 100 monthly credits plus daily credits, with higher tiers for more credits.
From about $50 a month with team workspaces, single sign-on and data opt-out.
Usage-based charges for hosting, database and AI features in published apps.
Extra credits when monthly ones run out.

businessModel.pricing: Free: a few credits a day. Pro: from about $25 a month. Business: from about $50 a month. Enterprise: custom. Cloud and AI usage billed by use above a free allowance. Prices from lovable.dev and may change.
costDrivers: AI model costs paid to Anthropic, OpenAI and Google for every message
Hosting and database costs for published apps
Small but highly paid engineering team
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Pro user pays about $25 a month. If they use all 100 or so credits, each message might cost Lovable a few cents to tens of cents in AI fees, so model costs could be $5 to 15. That leaves a gross margin of maybe 40 to 70%, lower than normal software because AI costs are high. Users who loop on bugs burn credits and cost more, but they also often buy top-ups. Lovable's tiny team of about 146 people keeps other costs low.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral demos on X, LinkedIn and YouTube of apps built in minutes
Users sharing apps with a 'Built with Lovable' link
Word of mouth among founders and PMs
whatBringsUsersBack: Live apps that need updates and new features
Credits refresh every month, encouraging use
Hosting on Lovable Cloud keeps apps on the platform
New AI models make the builder better every few months
growth.moat: Lovable's moat is still forming. Its brand and community are strong, and apps hosted on Lovable Cloud create switching costs. But it relies on the same AI models as rivals, so the core building ability is easy to copy. Speed of shipping and ease of use are its main defences.

northStar.metric: Apps published and used by real end users each week
northStar.why: A published app that other people use means the builder created real value. It filters out abandoned experiments and links to retention and revenue. Guardrail metrics make sure growth does not come at the cost of trust, safety or margins.

Owns hosting and backend through Lovable Cloud

Apps built by beginners can have security holes

Security scandal from a data leak in a popular Lovable app

improvementIdeas.idea: Do not charge credits for failed automatic fix attempts
improvementIdeas.problem: Users feel cheated when credits are used on the AI's own mistakes.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher trust, fewer complaints and lower churn.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Monthly paid churn and complaint rate about credits

improvementIdeas.idea: Plan mode that writes a simple step-by-step plan before big changes
improvementIdeas.problem: Large changes cause errors and loops.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher success rate for complex requests.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Error rate per prompt and fix loop rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Mandatory security check with plain-English fixes before publishing
improvementIdeas.problem: Beginners publish apps that leak user data.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer security incidents and more enterprise trust.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Security incidents per thousand published apps

improvementIdeas.idea: Lower-priced plan for India and emerging markets
improvementIdeas.problem: $25 a month is a lot for students and small businesses in India.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More paying users in large markets.

improvementIdeas.idea: Built-in analytics for every published app
improvementIdeas.problem: Builders do not know if anyone uses their app, so they stop.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More app updates and longer subscriptions.

pmLessons: Time to 'wow' wins. Seeing a working app in a minute is what made Lovable spread.
AI costs shape pricing. Credits link price to cost, but feel unfair when the AI fails.
A new audience can be bigger than the old one. Lovable grew by serving non-coders, not developers.
Small teams can scale fast when AI and users do much of the work.
Quick growth needs quality and safety. Security problems can undo trust fast.

interviewQuestions.question: Lovable users complain about credits wasted on bug loops. How would you fix this?
interviewQuestions.hint: Size the problem with data. Options: free retries, better error detection, plan mode, refunds. Weigh cost to Lovable against churn. Pick a metric.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Lovable's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Avoid sign-ups or revenue alone. Suggest published apps with real users. Break into activation, build success, publish and usage.

interviewQuestions.question: How would Lovable win enterprise customers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Identify buyers (PM and design teams). Needs: security, single sign-on, matching tech stack, collaboration. Plan a pilot and success metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: OpenAI launches a free app builder in ChatGPT. What does Lovable do?
interviewQuestions.hint: What is unique: hosting, backend, community, focus. Double down there. Consider pricing and partnerships.

interviewQuestions.question: Many users build one app then leave. How would you improve retention?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment by goal. Ideas: analytics, templates for next app, team features, hosting value. Track month 2 and 3 retention.
